After dropping Game 1 of their wild-card series to the Chicago White Sox while throwing a bullpen day, the Houston Astros had to feel a sense of relief knowing they were turning to their ace, Hunter Brown, for Game 2.
But as the second inning came around on Wednesday, Brown had already been chased from the contest.
Chicago sent 10 batters to the plate in a four-run first, tagging Brown for five hits as it looked to win its first playoff series since 2005.
Brown managed to get two outs — both by way of the strikeout — before manager Joe Espada made the move to the bullpen.
White Sox leadoff hitter Sam Antonacci wasted little time putting Brown on his back foot, opening the game with a double that went off Astros left fielder Yordan Alvarez's glove. Kyle Teel then brought home Antonacci with a single, Miguel Vargas reached on an error, Andrew Benintendi scored both with a single and Tristan Peters completed the rally with an RBI single of his own.
Brown left with the bases loaded and two out, but Tuesday's opener, AJ Blubaugh, entered and escaped the jam.
Houston's pitching staff has been ravaged by injuries this season, leaving the 28-year-old Brown and Hayden Wesneski as their lone healthy starters for the playoffs.
With the Astros not clinching their AL West title until the final day of the regular season, they weren't able to line up their pitching staff, which led to the bullpen day in Game 1 before Brown and Wesneski could return on normal rest.
"Having those guys healthy with regular rest, it's super valuable for us," Espdada said before the series began, making Brown's short start all the more costly for an Astros team already needing length from their pitchers.
Brown finished the 2026 regular season with a 3.19 ERA and 124 strikeouts over 107.1 innings. He was also hit by the injury bug earlier in the season, which limited the six-foot-two right-hander to just 20 starts.

Pete Crow-Armstrong's historic season just produced another staggering number, this time away from the baseball field.
The Chicago Cubs star's one-of-one 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph sold for $1.098 million at Goldin.
The PSA Gem Mint 10 card, which also received a PSA 10 autograph grade, features the MLB Debut patch from Crow-Armstrong's first major-league game on September 11, 2023.
It is a massive sale by itself.
The timing makes it even more striking.
Crow-Armstrong just completed a historic 40-home run, 40-stolen base season and helped Chicago reach the postseason. Now, only days later, his signature rookie card has approached the MLB Debut Patch record while Crow-Armstrong and the Cubs enter an elimination game against the San Diego Padres.
$1,098,000: Winning bid for Pete Crow-Armstrong’s debut patch jersey tonight at @GoldinCo.
PCA’s 2024 rookie salary: $740,000. pic.twitter.com/d21WopsNpx
— Darren Rovell (@darrenrovell) September 30, 2026
Pete Crow-Armstrong Card Sells for $1.098 Million
Crow-Armstrong's card was one of the most significant MLB Debut Patch cards to reach the market since Paul Skenes' one-of-one sold in 2025.
Goldin listed the card as Crow-Armstrong's 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph 1/1, graded PSA Gem Mint 10 with a PSA/DNA Gem Mint 10 autograph grade.
The $1.098 million result also produced a remarkable comparison highlighted by Rovell.
Crow-Armstrong earned roughly $740,000 during the 2024 season, meaning a collector just paid considerably more for his one-of-one rookie card than the Cubs paid Crow-Armstrong to play an entire major-league season.
But the final auction price may be even more notable for what it narrowly failed to accomplish.
Pete Crow-Armstrong Falls $12,000 Short of Paul Skenes Record
Crow-Armstrong came extraordinarily close to taking down the benchmark for MLB Debut Patch cards.
Skenes' one-of-one 2024 Topps Chrome Update MLB Debut Patch Autograph sold for $1.11 million through Fanatics Collect in March 2025. The price included the buyer's premium and established the Skenes card as the highest-selling MLB Debut Patch at the time.
Crow-Armstrong finished at $1.098 million.
The difference?
Just $12,000.
That puts Crow-Armstrong and Skenes in remarkably similar territory despite playing dramatically different positions and arriving in the majors with different levels of prospect hype.
Skenes was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 MLB Draft and won National League Rookie of the Year in his first season. His Debut Patch became a national story even before it surfaced, with the Pittsburgh Pirates famously offering the young collector who pulled it a package that included 30 years of season tickets.
Crow-Armstrong's card reached seven figures after a different catalyst: one of the greatest individual seasons ever produced by a Cubs player.
Pete Crow-Armstrong Made Cubs History Before $1.1 Million Sale
The auction could hardly have closed at a better moment for Crow-Armstrong's hobby profile.
On September 24, Crow-Armstrong stole his 40th base of the season, joining the exclusive 40-40 club after already reaching 45 home runs.
He became just the seventh player in MLB history to record at least 40 homers and 40 stolen bases in the same season. He also became the first Cubs player to accomplish the feat.
And he did it on the same night Chicago clinched an NL Wild Card berth with a 2-1 victory over the Miami Marlins.
Crow-Armstrong entered the postseason hitting .280 with 45 home runs and 107 RBIs while appearing in all 159 Cubs games through the clinching victory.
That transformed the timing of the Goldin auction.
Collectors were not merely bidding on the Debut Patch of a promising young Cubs player.
They were bidding on the Debut Patch of a 24-year-old who had just completed the first 40-40 season in franchise history.
Now the attention shifts back to what Crow-Armstrong can do on the field.
Cubs Face Elimination Against Padres After 8-0 Loss
Chicago enters Game 2 of its Wild Card Series against San Diego needing a victory to keep its season alive.
The Padres routed the Cubs 8-0 in Game 1 on September 29.
San Diego starter Michael King took a no-hit bid into the seventh inning and ultimately allowed only one hit over seven scoreless frames while striking out eight. Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado and Xander Bogaerts each homered for the Padres.
The Cubs will send Kevin Gausman to the mound for Game 2 opposite Nick Pivetta
There is at least one reason for optimism surrounding Crow-Armstrong specifically.
Chicago dominated San Diego during the regular season, winning five of six games and outscoring the Padres 55-28.
Crow-Armstrong was one of the Cubs' biggest problems for San Diego.
He hit .364 with four home runs in the six regular-season meetings.
Chicago will need another performance like that now.
Crow-Armstrong has already produced one of the defining baseball-card sales of 2026 and one of the most statistically significant seasons in Cubs history.
Whether his week is remembered primarily for a $1.098 million card sale or for what happens in October now depends on what Crow-Armstrong and the Cubs do next.

Pete Crow-Armstrong Joins Elite Company: The 7 Players In The 40/40 Club
24-year-old Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong joined one of the rarest clubs in Major League Baseball this season. The NL MVP favorite became the seventh player in MLB history to hit 40+ home runs and steal 40+ bases in a single season.
While there are only a select few talented players who have made the club, there are several players from this generation who have made the cut and also invented clubs of their own.
Here is a list of the 7 players to make the 40/40 club:
RELATED | Top 20 All-Time Greatest Baseball Players
RELATED | MLB Players Who Played In The Little League World Series
1988 Jose Canseco – 42 HR, 40 SB, .307 AVG, .391 OBP, .569 SLG
The founding member of this club, Canseco, predicted he would achieve this milestone. He also drove in a league-leading 124 runs and posted a heavy .569 slugging percentage to coast to a unanimous AL MVP.
Canseco would lose to the Dodgers 4-1 in the World Series, winning the only game with a grand
1996 Barry Bonds – 42 HR, 40 SB, .308 AVG, .461 OBP, .615 SLG
Bonds paired pure athleticism with legendary plate discipline, combining 42 home runs and 40 stolen bases with a career-high 151 walks.
His absurd .461 OBP ensured he was constantly on base to leverage his speed, though his 9.7 WAR effort incredibly finished fifth in a hitter-dominated NL MVP vote that season.
Even with Bonds’ historic run, the Giant’s struggled this season, finishing 68-94 and 4th in the NL West.
1998 Alex Rodriguez – 42 HR, 46 SB, .310 AVG, .360 OBP, .560 SLG
At just 22 years old, A-Rod accomplished what remains the most physically demanding 40/40 season by doing it as a everyday shortstop.
He recorded an MLB-leading 213 hits, which helped him finish the season with a 43.9 Power/Speed number—the highest mark ever achieved in baseball history.
Rodriguez’s Mariners failed to reach the playoffs as well, ending the season at 76-85 and 3rd in the AL West.
2006 Alfonso Soriano – 46 HR, 41 SB, .277 AVG, .351 OBP, .560 SLG
After coming just one home run short with the Yankees in 2002, Soriano left no doubt during his single, explosive season in Washington.
He blasted 46 home runs and swiped 41 bags. Soriano’s season stands out unique because he also hit 41 doubles, creating the game’s only 40/40/40 performance.
The Nationals also failed to reach the postseason, finishing 71-91 and 5th in the NL East.
2023 Ronald Acuna Jr. – 41 HR, 73 SB, .337 AVG, .416 OBP, .596 SLG
Acuña weaponized MLB’s larger bases and rules limiting pitcher disengagements to turn the 40/40 club completely on its head.
While maintaining a career-best .337 batting average, he bashed 41 home runs and ran wild for 73 stolen bases, easily taking home NL MVP honors.
After Acuna’s record-breaking season, the superstar struggled in the postseason, hitting 2-14 and only scoring two runs. The Braves would fall in the NLDS to the Philadelphia Phillies.
2024 Shohei Ohtani – 54 HR, 59 SB, .310 AVG, .390 OBP, .646 SLG
Serving strictly as a designated hitter while rehabbing his throwing arm, Ohtani reached 40/40 in a blistering 126 games—shattering Soriano’s previous speed record of 147 games. He hit a walk-off grand slam to secure the milestone, eventually pushing his totals to 54 home runs and 59 steals to create the 50/50 club.
Ohtani is the only player so far to cap off his historic season winning the World Series, beating the Yankees in 5 games.
2026 Pete Crow-Armstrong – 45 HR, 41 SB, .280 AVG, .372 OBP, .570 SLG
Originally known as a spectacular, defense-first center fielder, PCA shocked the baseball world by developing top-tier power to accompany his elite speed. He tied for the MLB lead with 45 home runs and secured his 40th stolen base during the Cubs’ playoff-clinching victory in late September.
The Chicago Cubs will play in the Wild Card round on Tuesday.
Who do you think had the most impressive season? Let us know!

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox starter in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card series on Wednesday needs no introduction to the boo birds. He’s got plenty of familiarity with the Bronx cheer, unfortunately for him, coming from his time with the Yankees.
Sonny Gray will toe the slab for Chad Tracy’s squad in a pivotal playoff game back in the place that was home to arguably the lowest point of his MLB career.
“I came from Oakland, and Oakland to [New York]. I think that maybe during my time there was a lot of outside this, outside that, unfamiliarity with me and my situation and my family,” Gray said before Tuesday’s Game 1. “It’s kind of like one of those things that you have a snowball or whatever, right?
“And there’s a snowball that kind of starts rolling down a hill. If you don’t ever stop it, then the snowball just gets bigger and bigger and bigger, and it picks up traction, and it just gets more snow. And it just continues to go down this thing. And then the bigger the snowball gets, the harder it is to stop it or take a step back.
“And for me, it just took me to get away and get myself into a different environment and then reflect on those things, right, like reflect on what was good, what was bad, what didn’t work. And that took some time.”
Gray pitched 41 games during his season-and-a-half with the Bombers — 4.51 ERA — and Yankee faithful will surely remember his time with the team on Wednesday.
The veteran starter is expecting the obvious in terms of the reception he’ll receive as he goes out to try and win a postseason game for the Red Sox.
“I think it will be a playoff energy on the road, playoff atmosphere on the road,” said Gray. “As far as reception, this or that, it will be what it will be. I’m not going to sit here and try to control something that I can’t control because I ultimately have no control over that.
“It will be what it will be, and I’ll just do my part to be ready to go out there and compete and to pitch and to go win a game.”
Gray was acquired from the Athletics at the 2017 trade deadline prior to the Bombers’ unexpected and memorable run to Game 7 of the ALCS. The 36-year-old was acquired to be a frontline starter behind Luis Severino at the very beginning of the ‘Baby Bombers’ era.
The right-hander’s first run with the Yanks was respectable as he pitched to a 3.72 ERA in 11 games during the 2017 season and even added a strong ALCS start, throwing five innings and allowing one earned run against the Houston Astros. However, the wheels fell off in 2018, when he owned a 4.90 ERA in 30 games and heard an awful amount of boos from the home crowd before being shipped off to the Cincinnati Reds in the offseason.
Despite the rough experience, Gray greatly values his time in New York and attributes it not only to the pitcher, but to the man he is today.
“I do know that playing here made me a stronger person, made me a better man, a better husband. Ultimately, it made me a better pitcher, a better baseball player. And that’s kind of what I take from my time here. …
“I learned a lot. I learned what to do, what not to do. I mean, it was a bump in the road for me, but ultimately it made me a better person.”
Gray found success immediately after departing the Bronx. He was an All-Star for the Reds in 2019 and then again with the Minnesota Twins in 2023. The veteran enters the postseason riding a very successful season in which he pitched to a 2.72 ERA in 29 games with the Red Sox.
The Tennessean is not focused on any sort of revenge and doesn’t need any added motivation to stick it to the Yankees. Instead, he’s solely focused on trying to win for the Bo Sox.
“That’s kind of how I look at it. I don’t look at it as any other thing than that.”

The Red Sox paid a handsome price for former Orioles catcher Adley Rutschman at the MLB trade deadline, dealing a handful of top prospects for the former No. 1 overall pick. After a middling second half, Chad Tracy’s first playoff lineup decision as manager of the Red Sox puts a lot of faith in Rutschman.
Tracy unveiled the Red Sox starting lineup that would hit against Yankees ace and likely Cy Young Cam Schlittler in Game 1 of the American League Wild Card at Yankee Stadium. Unsurprisingly, former top overall prospect in baseball Roman Anthony is leading off, but it’s Rutschman batting second ahead of All-Star first baseman Willson Contreras in the #3 spot.
Rutschman’s place in the order had been messed around with in the final days of the regular season, with Rutschman batting second, third or fifth on a given night. Much of Rutschman’s batting second has to do with the loss of Mickey Gasper to a biceps injury, as Gasper was usually the guy Tracy wanted on base ahead of the Red Sox’ power bats.
Chad Tracy’s Informed Adley Rutschman Lineup Decision
The decision to bat Rutschman second isn’t arbitrary: Rutschman is one of just two Red Sox players currently to have an extra base hit against Schlittler this year, along with third baseman Caleb Durbin, who hit a two-run home run against him earlier this season.
The Red Sox’ starting nine of Anthony, Rutschman, Contreras, Wilyer Abreu, Ceddanne Rafaela, Nick Sogard, Jarren Duran, Trevor Story and Durbin is just a combined 8-for-59 (.136) with the two extra base hits against Schlittler this season.
The lineup appears to be Chad Tracy’s best attempt at getting some runs across against Schlittler. The announcement comes amid musings that the Red Sox reportedly “wore out” the Rays’ Trajekt machine mimicking Schlittler’s arsenal this weekend while they were playing their season finale against the Cubs in the domed Tropicana Field due to heavy rain in Boston.
AL Wild Card Preview
The Yankees put out a platoon-heavy lineup of their own, starting veterans Paul Goldschmidt and Amed Rosario over Luis Garcia Jr. at first and Jazz Chisholm Jr at second. The Yankees got a “mini break” as their games against the Orioles on Saturday and Sunday, with no clinching scenarios on the line, were canceled due to the same nor’easter that pushed the Sox and Cubs to Florida.
It’ll be a rematch of the 2025 American League Wild Card series, which the Yankees won in three electrifying games, but with a different cast of characters, Rutschman chief among them. The Red Sox will surely rely on him finding his bat this series after posting a disappointing .222/.278/.410 slash in the final two months of the season after the trade from Baltimore. He’ll be thrown immediately into the fire against Schlittler, and it should certainly be a fun one.

The Houston Astros enter the postseason with the AL MVP favorite in their lineup.
Yordan Alvarez should be considered the most feared hitter in baseball for this year's playoffs.
But the rest of Houston's lineup has been mediocre at best.
"The Astros have the presumptive AL MVP in Yordan Alvarez, but the rest of the offense has produced a .233/.300/.396 line this year," Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter wrote. "He will need to replicate his memorable performance in the 2023 ALCS for pretty much the entirety of October."
Clearly, the Astros rely on Alvarez to do most of their offensive damage, but he may not be the AL West club's "X-Factor" during the Wild Card Series against the Chicago White Sox.
Instead, Reuter has tabbed rookie center fielder Lucas Spence as someone who can help Houston make a deep postseason run.
"Lucas Spence went 6-for-18 with four home runs in five games after being recalled from Triple-A when [Daulton] Varsho and [Brice] Matthews were placed on the injured list," Reuter added. "He suddenly looks like the no-doubt starting center fielder for the club's playoff run."
MORE: Pirates urged to re-sign Brandon Lowe if they ‘want to be taken seriously’
Varsho is unavailable in the Wild Card Series due to left wrist inflammation caused by cysts.
He is a Gold Glove outfielder but has hit poorly following a midseason trade from the Toronto Blue Jays.
Spence has just 19 MLB games under his belt but looks up for the challenge, hitting the first three home runs of his career in a single game during the last week of the regular season against the Athletics.

As the 2026 MLB postseason prepares to begin, it's a good time for some bold predictions about who will win and why, from the wild-card rounds to the World Series.
Chicago White Sox at Houston Astros
Houston was just 11-13 in September and it felt like neither the Astros nor the Texas Rangers wanted to win the AL West. Houston finally did on the last day, but the Astros aren't inspiring confidence that they can go deep into the postseason.
The White Sox could have been the AL Central champs, but couldn't hang on as Cleveland made a hard charge and overtook them. For a team that has been told all season about they are still living in the shadow of a 121-loss season two years ago, this team has a chip on its shoulder. That should push the White Sox into the next round.
Boston Red Sox at New York Yankees
After a chaotic weather weekend in the Northeast that forced the Red Sox to play Game 162 in Tampa and canceled the final game of the season for the Yankees, that extra day of rest (and far less travel) may help New York when the wild-card series opens in the Bronx.
New York's pitching lineup of Cam Schlittler, Max Fried and Gerrit Cole will be enough to overcome any of the Yankees' offensive issues in a series that will last just two games.
Philadelphia Phillies at Atlanta Braves
Like Houston, Philadelphia did little to inspire confidence in its postseason future at the end of the regular season. It's also been a season where the Braves have Philadelphia's number, winning nine of the 13 games the two rivals have played. Atlanta sweeps Philadelphia.
Chicago Cubs at San Diego Padres
The Padres are red-hot entering the wild card, going 18-6 in September to secure a home series. Having the home fans on their side, San Diego will continue its solid play by sweeping the Cubs into the offseason.
New York Yankees vs. Tampa Bay Rays
While the Yankees may have had enough to get into the ALDS, there's little doubt that the Rays are the better team.
All season, it was a question of if New York could catch Tampa Bay for the AL East title. The Rays kept showing they weren't going to crack under any pressure, and that continues with a 3-1 series win to move on to the ALCS.
Chicago White Sox vs. Cleveland Guardians
Chicago's story has been incredible, but there's a reason why the Guardians won the division ... and keep a reputation as the team that doesn't die easily. They're built for pressure and the postseason and will dispatch the White Sox in four games.
Atlanta Braves vs. Los Angeles Dodgers
This will be must-see TV as two of the NL's behemoths battle it out. The home advantage will make a difference for the Dodgers, who will win in Game 5 to seal another trip to the NLCS.
San Diego Padres vs. Milwaukee Brewers
Milwaukee is for real. There have been plenty of instances in the past where the Brewers have stumbled in the postseason, but this won't be a repeat of those mistakes. Jacob Misiorowski will set the tone in the first game and the Brewers will win in four.
Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians
The Rays went 5-1 against Cleveland this season. With homefield advantage, there's no reason to think that trend won't continue. Look for the Rays to oust the Guardians in six games.
Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Milwaukee Brewers
This season, the Brewers are 4-3 against the Dodgers. With Milwaukee holding home-field advantage, this is the year that Los Angeles is finally stopped short of winning it all.
There is a lot to like for Milwaukee in their relief pitching options, and it may come down to that. While the Dodgers may have the better rotation, Milwaukee has the better pitching staff overall. Pitching wins in October, and the Brewers win a classic in seven games in front of their home fans.
Tampa Bay Rays vs. Milwaukee Brewers
A World Series without a "major market" in it? Oh this will set up plenty of conversations for what will be a contentious offseason.
Neither of these teams have won a World Series, making for another fascinating storyline in what will be an epic Fall Classic. Milwaukee has the home-field advantage thanks to their 103 regular-season wins, and that makes a big difference in this battle of the top seeds.
Brewers in six.
